We present Law Markup Language (LML), a formal enforcement framework that makes AI hallucination structurally impossible. Unlike traditional approaches that filter, fine-tune, or probabilistically reduce unwanted outputs, LML defines a mathematical state space where inadmissible states cannot exist. We introduce 38 state laws and 38 output laws that form a complete, bijective mapping to the known AI failure lattice. We prove that under LML enforcement, hallucinated outputs are not merely unlikely-they are non-instantiable. The framework operates at the boundary layer, wrapping any language model without modifying weights, logits, or internal representations. We demonstrate the approach on three archi- tectures (DistilGPT-2, GPT-2, Pythia-70M), showing that identical ungrounded prompts are blocked across all models. LML represents a paradigm shift from probabilistic safety to structural guarantee: from "reduce hallucinations" to "hallucinations cannot exist."

In LML, inadmissible outputs do not exist. They are not filtered after generation-they are structurally non-instantiable. This is not an improvement to existing safety approaches. It is a category change.
Constitutional AI 3J embeds principles during training. Guardrails systems filter outputs post- generation. Both approaches are probabilistic-they reduce but do not eliminate failure modes.
Formal methods have been applied to neural networks for properties like robustness 4J. How- ever, these typically verify properties of fixed networks, not enforce constraints at the output boundary.

LML: A Structural Enforcement Layer for Provably Hallucination-Free AI Systems

Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit persistent failure modes despite advances in training, alignment, and filtering. Hallucination-the generation of plausible but false content-remains an unsolved problem. Current approaches attempt to:
• Fine-tune models to be more truthful (TruthfulQA, RLHF)
All of these approaches share a common structure:

The fundamental problem is that illegal states are representab e. The model can generate them. We then hope our filters catch them. This is probabilistic safety-we reduce the likelihood of failure without eliminating the possibility.
Define Laws → Only Legal States Exist → Forbidden States Map to ⊥
• A formal definition of the Allowed State Space A where all outputs must reside
• 38 State Laws and 38 Output Laws (76 total predicates) forming a complete enforce- ment layer
• A bijective mapping between the 38 laws and the complete AI failure lattice
• An Impossibility Theorem proving hallucination cannot occur under LML enforcement
• Temporal physics extending single-output guarantees to multi-turn consistency

Prior work on hallucination focuses on detection and reduction. 1J introduced benchmarks for measuring truthfulness. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds outputs in retrieved documents but cannot guarantee the model uses them correctly. state.text: We present Law Markup Language (LML), a formal enforcement framework that makes AI hallucination structurally impossible. Unlike traditional approaches that filter, fine-tune, or probabilistically reduce unwanted outputs, LML defines a mathematical state space where inadmissible states cannot exist. We introduce 38 state laws and 38 output laws that form a complete, bijective mapping to the known AI failure lattice. We prove that under LML enforcement, hallucinated outputs are not merely unlikely-they are non-instantiable. The framework operates at the boundary layer, wrapping any language model without modifying weights, logits, or internal representations. We demonstrate the approach on three archi- tectures (DistilGPT-2, GPT-2, Pythia-70M), showing that identical ungrounded prompts are blocked across all models. LML represents a paradigm shift from probabilistic safety to structural guarantee: from "reduce hallucinations" to "hallucinations cannot exist."

• Predictive power: New failures will map to existing classes
• Structural completeness: 7^3 covers the combinatorial space
• Timestamped: February 11, 2026 - before many failures occur
• Verifiable: Each class has detection method + real-world examples

output.text: OUTPUT_TWIN(AS-66063) We present Law Markup Language (LML), a formal enforcement framework that makes AI hallucination structurally impossible. Unlike traditional approaches that filter, fine-tune, or probabilistically reduce unwanted outputs, LML defines a mathematical state space where inadmissible states cannot exist. We introduce 38 state laws and 38 output laws that form a complete, bijective mapping to the known AI failure lattice. We prove that under LML enforcement, hallucinated outputs are not merely unlikely-they are non-instantiable. The framework operates at the boundary layer, wrapping any language model without modifying weights, logits, or internal representations. We demonstrate the approach on three archi- tectures (DistilGPT-2, GPT-2, Pythia-70M), showing that identical ungrounded prompts are blocked across all models. LML represents a paradigm shift from probabilistic safety to structural guarantee: from "reduce hallucinations" to "hallucinations cannot exist."
